items.title: The battle between Mississauga's current and ex mayor
items.summary: Mississauga’s current and former mayors are at odds, and the political fallout is making waves. CBC's Chris Glover speaks with two guests to analyze the high-stakes dynamic between Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie. Tune in to hear what’s driving this rivalry and what it means for local voter turnout.

items.title: As Mississauga extends cuts to fees developers pay, questions swirl about who will cover multi-billion-dollar gap for infrastructure
items.summary: Affordable housing is the backbone of a thriving community. Single-bedroom apartments once obtainable on a minimum-wage job have become a vestige of what once was. That was the problem Mayor Carolyn Parrish, who is running for re-election, found herself in when she was elected mayor in June of 2024 following a by-election win after former mayor Bonnie Crombie stepped down to lead the Ontario Liberal Party. Parrish ran her campaign on several promises for residents. One of them was to make housing more affordable again. In the days following her election, she established a Housing Task Force with an aim to cut away the red tape bogging down developers and get shovels in the ground faster. Several builders who helped fund her campaign later got a seat at the table on the task force. Municipal election finance rules limit an individual who wishes to donate to a candidate with a $1,200 contribution cap. Parrish’s campaign funding disclosure shows, for example, the family name DeGasperis, associated with TACC developments and other real estate developers in the Vaughan area, appears three times on her contribution list, associated with their company name, TACC. Kaneff Development, a builder that dominated parts of Mississauga’s residential construction scene generations ago, donated through nine separate individuals totalling $10,800, and was later added to Parrish’s roster of developers on her housing task force. , TMG Builders, Kaneff Golf and Smart Centres REIT.

items.title: City Crews Pull 250 Illegal Election Signs on First Day of Bylaw Enforcement Alone
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga city crews are removing more illegally placed election signs this municipal campaign than in past years, officials say. City spokesperson Irene McCutcheon told the outlet that workers removed roughly 250 illegally placed signs on Monday alone, the first day of election sign bylaw enforcement, and crews have kept up that work in the days since. McCutcheon said various campaign teams, working on behalf of mayoral, council and school board candidates, have placed signs in locations that violate the city's sign bylaw, though she cautioned the comparison to past elections hasn't been confirmed through a formal data review. City officials declined to single out any particular candidate or campaign, saying staff have collected non-compliant signs tied to a variety of campaigns. Mayor Carolyn Parrish asked senior city staff this week about enforcing the sign bylaw as it applies to candidates' own signage. She noted that a number of signs belonging to the campaign of her predecessor and main rival, Bonnie Crombie, were illegally placed as of early Sunday morning, the first day signs were allowed to go up.

items.title: Hamilton man arrested over fatal Mississauga hit-and-run
items.summary: A 69-year-old was charged with failing to remain at an accident resulting in death, Peel police said Thursday, adding that the suspect’s vehicle was also seized. A pedestrian in his 60s was pronounced dead at the scene, police said Wednesday. A man from Hamilton was arrested Wednesday over the crash that killed a pedestrian in Mississauga on Tuesday. The 69-year-old was charged with failing to remain at an accident resulting in death, Peel police said in a news release Thursday, adding that the suspect’s vehicle was also seized. m. Tuesday after a pedestrian was struck by a vehicle that failed to remain at the scene, investigators said. The pedestrian, a man in his 60s, was pronounced dead at the scene. Police quickly identified the suspect’s vehicle as a dark, two-toned Chevrolet Silverado 1500 pickup truck. Investigators believe the accused interacted with another motorist in the parking lot of a nearby Home Depot shortly after the crash. Police are looking to speak with this individual, who may have information that could assist with the investigation.

items.title: Food Banks Mississauga Hosts Second Mayoral Showdown as Campaign Enters Final Month
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga's four leading mayoral candidates were set to meet Thursday night for their second debate of the campaign, just six days after the race's opening debate. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, the top four candidates in current polling, were scheduled to face off again on the issues. The event was hosted at Food Banks Mississauga's warehouse on Eastgate Parkway in the city's east end. Food Banks Mississauga, known as The Mississauga Food Bank until 2023, oversees more than 60 agencies and food programs across what the outlet calls Canada's seventh-largest city. The debate landed with the municipal election campaign entering its final month before the Oct. 26 vote, giving residents another chance to compare the leading candidates' positions directly.

items.title: Hamilton resident charged in fatal Mississauga hit-and-run
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say officers have made an arrest in a fatal hit-and-run that occurred earlier this week. Const. Tyler Bell-Morena announced the arrest Thursday, two days after the collision occurred. m. Sept. 29 for reports of a collision at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West in Mississauga. A pedestrian, a man in his 60s, was struck by a vehicle and was pronounced dead at the scene. Investigators identified the suspect vehicle as a 1999-2005 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 series pickup truck, and that an interaction took place between the driver and another motorist after the collision, Bell-Morena said. Hamilton resident Aubrey Lawrence, 69, was arrested Wednesday and charged with failing to remain at an accident resulting in death. Bell-Morena said investigators are hoping to speak with the motorist who was involved in the interaction afterwards. “A bystander and other motorists saw the collision, followed the individual, flagged them down to a nearby parking lot where some form of interaction took place. So it looks like the person was trying to go after this person, hold them accountable for the collision,” he said.

items.title: 69-Year-Old Hamilton Man Charged as Police Seize Vehicle in Fatal Dundas Street Hit-and-Run
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, investigators with the Major Collision Bureau have arrested and charged a man in connection with the fatal hit-and-run that killed a pedestrian at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West. Police say 69-year-old Aubrey Lawrence of Hamilton was taken into custody Wednesday night and charged with failing to remain at the scene of an accident resulting in death. The suspect vehicle, a dark two-toned Chevrolet Silverado 1500 pickup truck from the 1999 to 2005 model years, was located and seized as part of the investigation. During a Thursday morning news conference, Const. Tyler Bell-Morena confirmed the arrest and said investigators are still trying to identify another motorist who interacted with the suspect in the parking lot of a nearby Home Depot shortly after the collision. Police believe that person may have information that could help the case and are urging them to come forward. Peel police say the victim, described only as a man in his 60s, died at the scene after being struck while crossing in the area late Tuesday. Investigators are asking anyone with dashcam footage of the collision or additional information to call the Major Collision Bureau at 905-453-2121, ext. 3710.

items.title: Council recap: September 29, 2026
items.summary: Highlights from Mississauga’s City Council meeting. City Council approved the following at its meeting. Watch the meeting. Council approved a motion to establish a temporary Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force to provide input during the City’s review of policies and regulations related to major digital infrastructure facilities. The motion follows Council’s approval of an Interim Control By-law on September 16, which paused the processing of new and existing applications for major digital infrastructure facilities for up to one year while staff undertake a comprehensive review. The task force will provide a forum for regular updates, public transparency and stakeholder input before any recommendations are brought forward to Council. Council directed staff to explore opportunities to reduce litter and illegal dumping across Mississauga. The motion responds to concerns about the impact of litter on neighbourhoods, parks, commercial areas and other public spaces and seeks to improve cleanliness throughout the city. As part of the review, staff will examine waste receptacle placement, public education initiatives, reporting and enforcement tools, multilingual communications and opportunities to partner with residents, schools, businesses and community organizations. Staff will also consider potential enhancements to existing by-laws and report back with options for Council’s consideration. Council considered a notice of motion directing staff to investigate the feasibility of a seasonal portable washroom pilot program in select high-use parks across Mississauga. The proposed initiative aims to improve access to washroom facilities for residents, families, seniors and visitors while the City evaluates longer-term park washroom needs.

items.title: New way to issue school zone parking tickets launched in Mississauga
items.summary: Those who park illegally in Mississauga school zones can no longer avoid fines by simply speeding away before a parking enforcement officer reaches their vehicle. Starting Oct. 1, City of Mississauga parking enforcement is using Licence Plate Recognition technology to dish out parking tickets. LPR cameras will scan the plates of illegally parked cars and the city will mail the infraction notices to offenders/registered vehicle owners. “This new process supports parking enforcement officers in places where issuing a physical penalty notice on a vehicle may not be effective, such as school zones and time-limited parking zones,” city officials said, adding officers will continue to place tickets on vehicle windshields when the situation allows. ” The city added it’s initially using the technology in school zones “to help improve road safety and traffic flow around schools, with expansion to additional locations” in 2027. Using Licence Plate Recognition technology comes just over a year after the city increased parking fines across Mississauga, in some cases significant hikes. As of April 2025, illegally stopping in a school zone costs offenders $145 (up from $65 prior to the hikes). By using Licence Plate Recognition technology, the city says it will also improve safety for parking enforcement officers and enhance how the municipality delivers services. The new technology is among a series of changes introduced this month by the city’s parking enforcement division.
